faq.site.title: The website
faq.site.what.a: A free social information website. It brings together aids, procedures, places that welcome the public and guides, checked against official sources, to help you know what to check and whom to contact. It is not a government website: it does not replace the CAF, Health Insurance or France Travail.
faq.site.free.a: Yes. Access is free for individuals, with no advertising, no paid ranking and no sale of data.
faq.site.who.a: AccesDirectAide is a non-profit project run by a private individual. The planned association under the local law of Alsace-Moselle has not been created yet. Information about the publisher is in the legal notice.
faq.site.territory.a: Local information mainly concerns the Eurométropole de Strasbourg; national aids apply everywhere in France. The “Area covered” page details what is available.
faq.site.account.q: Do I need an account to use the website?
faq.site.account.a: No. Aids, procedures, places and guides can be read without an account. An account is only used for personal features (favourites, My Journey, appointments…), when they are open.
faq.find.title: Finding an aid, a procedure or a place
faq.find.search.q: How do I search for an aid?
faq.find.search.a: Type a few words into the search, for example “student rent”, or open the Aids page. You can filter by category, by situation and by area.
faq.find.near.q: Can I see what exists near me?
faq.find.near.a: Yes. In the search, choose your municipality: aids reserved for another area are no longer shown, and places in that municipality are listed first. In the directory, you can filter by town and by type of organisation, and show a map.
faq.find.demarche.q: Where can I find the steps of a procedure?
faq.find.demarche.a: The Procedures page explains administrative procedures step by step (for example a passport), with the link to the official source.
faq.find.place.q: How do I find a place that welcomes the public?
faq.find.place.a: The directory lists places: town halls, CCAS, CAF, France Services, associations… You can keep only the places accessible to people with reduced mobility, or those that offer online appointments.
faq.find.start.q: I don’t know where to start.
faq.find.start.a: Start from “Find help by need”: describe your situation in your own words or choose an area. The “My situation” page also suggests, depending on what is happening to you, the aids to check, the procedures and the places to contact.
faq.find.tools.q: What are the guides, the tools and the glossary for?
faq.find.tools.a: The Guides are written in plain language to help you prepare your procedures and appointments. The Tools link to simulators and online services chosen from the websites of public bodies. The Glossary explains acronyms and difficult words.
faq.rights.title: My rights
faq.rights.decide.q: Can the website tell me whether an aid is for me?
faq.rights.decide.a: No. The website helps you spot the aids that may concern you and know what to check. Only the body concerned (CAF, département, town hall…) decides, after examining your application.
faq.rights.conditions.q: What do the conditions written on a page mean?
faq.rights.conditions.a: They are the conditions published by the official source. They help you know whether it is worth checking, but they are not enough: the body examines your whole situation and decides.
faq.rights.page.a: Need by need, it presents the official Service-Public pages, the body that decides and the possible steps, with no questions and no account.
faq.rights.amount.q: Does the website calculate the amount of an aid?
faq.rights.amount.a: No. For an estimate, use the official simulators on the Tools page. Only the body sets the amount.
faq.rights.refused.q: My application was refused: what can I do?
faq.rights.refused.a: The decision belongs to the body. The reply letter usually states the possible appeals and their deadlines: read it carefully. A place that welcomes the public (CCAS, France Services, association) can help you: look for one in the directory.
faq.sources.title: Sources and checks
faq.sources.where.q: Where does the information come from?
faq.sources.where.a: Each page starts from a public source: Service-Public, the FINESS register, the Directory of the administration, local authority websites. The source is shown on the page.
faq.sources.date.a: It is the date of the last automatic check of the page against its official source. A page is published only after this check. If the source disappears or no longer confirms the information, the page is withdrawn until the next check.
faq.sources.conflict.q: The page and the official website say different things: which is right?
faq.sources.conflict.a: The official website is authoritative. Follow the link to the official source and tell us about the difference so that the page can be corrected.
faq.account.title: My account and My Space
faq.account.create.q: How do I create an account?
faq.account.create.a: Choose “Create an account”, enter your e-mail address and a password (at least 8 characters, including an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter and a digit), confirm that you are 18 or over, then open the verification link sent by e-mail. During the public beta, account creation is opening gradually.
faq.account.forgot.a: Use “Forgotten password”: if the address is known, a reset link is sent to it. If you no longer have access to your e-mail address, recovery help is offered on the same page.
faq.account.space.a: My Space brings your sections together: My Journey, My Vault, favourites, appointments, messages, shared files, referrals, trusted persons, assisted mode, history, profile and settings. Only the open sections are shown. To keep a page, use “Add to my favourites” on the page once signed in.
faq.account.parcours.a: To follow your procedures step by step: add a page with “Add to my pathway”, say where you stand and, if needed, a deadline. Sensitive steps (health, disability, residence, justice…) need your explicit consent. AccesDirectAide makes no decision about your rights.
faq.account.coffre.a: A space to keep your documents (PDF, PNG or JPEG, 3 MB at most), encrypted: only you have access. Do not upload medical documents until the page offers it. Files are not yet scanned by an antivirus.
faq.account.trusted.a: A relative or a representative you invite by e-mail. You choose what they can see (My Journey without your notes, the list of My Vault without opening the documents, your next appointments) and for how long, from 30 days to 1 year. You can end the access at any time.
faq.account.helper.a: It lets a person sitting next to you help you with your account, for 2 hours at most. You choose the sections that are opened and confirm with your password. This person can never change your password or your e-mail, nor delete your account.
faq.account.history.q: Does the website keep what I look at?
faq.account.history.a: Only if you turn on “My history”, which is optional. You can erase one entry or the whole history; turning it off erases everything.
faq.rdv.title: Appointments and messages
faq.rdv.book.q: Can I book an appointment online?
faq.rdv.book.a: Only with organisations that have opened online booking: their page then offers “See available time slots”. Otherwise, contact the organisation directly. You need an account with a verified e-mail address. Some organisations approve each request before confirming it. During the public beta, booking is opening gradually.
faq.rdv.change.q: How do I move or cancel an appointment?
faq.rdv.change.a: In My appointments. An appointment can be moved up to 24 hours before, twice at most. Cancelling notifies the organisation and cannot be undone. You can also add the appointment to your calendar.
faq.rdv.messages.a: Messaging is for exchanges linked to your appointments with an organisation. Messages are encrypted on our servers, but not end to end: do not write health information or identity numbers in them. Attachments are not open yet.
faq.rdv.share.q: How do I share a file with an organisation?
faq.rdv.share.a: From your files (My profile), choose a verified organisation. The invitation link works only once, for 72 hours. You can stop sharing at any time.
faq.rdv.orientation.q: An organisation offers to forward my file: what happens?
faq.rdv.orientation.a: The proposal appears in My referrals: you accept it or refuse it. Nothing is forwarded without your agreement, and the internal notes of organisations are never forwarded.
faq.data.title: Personal data and security
faq.data.collected.a: Nothing is asked of you to browse the website. With an account, it is the information you record yourself. The details (purposes, retention periods, recipients) are in the privacy policy.
faq.data.cookies.a: Mainly to keep you signed in, secure the website and keep your settings. No advertising, no social networks, no tracking from one website to another. The Cookies page gives the full list.
faq.data.security.q: Where is the data hosted and how is it protected?
faq.data.security.a: The “Security and GDPR” page presents the hosting and the protection measures.
faq.data.export.q: How do I download my data?
faq.data.export.a: In the account settings, “Download (JSON)” produces a file with your data. There you can also ask to restrict the use of your data or object to it.
faq.data.delete.q: How do I delete my account?
faq.data.delete.a: Ask for deletion in the account settings. The account stays active until the request is processed; deletion is then final, except for data the law requires to be kept.
faq.data.sensitive.q: What should I avoid writing on the website?
faq.data.sensitive.a: Do not write sensitive information (health, social security number, identity documents) in a message, a report or an e-mail.
faq.a11y.title: Accessibility and languages
faq.a11y.display.q: How do I enlarge the text or change the colours?
faq.a11y.display.a: The “Accessibility” button at the top of the page sets the text size (from 80% to 150%), the contrast, the line spacing and an easy reading mode. Another button switches between dark and light mode. Settings stay on your device.
faq.a11y.falc.a: Yes, for some pages: turn on the easy-to-read version (FALC, in French). A simplified text that is still provisional is marked as such.
faq.a11y.listen.q: Can the website read the page aloud?
faq.a11y.listen.a: Yes: “Listen to the page” uses your device’s speech synthesis. You can read the page, a section or a selected text, and set the speed.
faq.a11y.languages.q: In which languages is the website available?
faq.a11y.languages.a: French, English, Turkish, Arabic (read right to left), German and Ukrainian. The interface is translated; a page is translated automatically when the translation has passed the checks, otherwise it stays in French. The French text and the official source are authoritative.
faq.a11y.hide.q: How do I hide the screen quickly?
faq.a11y.hide.a: Use the “Hide the screen” button or press Escape three times: a dark screen covers the page. Click to bring it back. Note: this does not erase your browser history.
faq.compass.title: Boussole sociale
faq.compass.what.a: An automatic assistant that answers your questions using only verified official sources: without a verified source, it does not answer. It answers in French. It can be wrong: always check on the official page.
faq.compass.decide.q: Does the Boussole decide instead of the body?
faq.compass.decide.a: No. Its answers are not a decision: only the body concerned decides.
faq.compass.commune.q: Why does the Boussole ask for my municipality?
faq.compass.commune.a: Aid and places often depend on where you live. When your question needs it, the Boussole asks for your municipality: type its name (for example “Strasbourg”) or a sentence such as “I live in Schiltigheim”. With a postcode, it lets you choose the municipality.
faq.compass.missing.q: I can’t see the Boussole: why?
faq.compass.missing.a: During the public beta, the assistant is opening gradually: if it is not shown, it is not open yet. The pages, the search and “Find help by need” remain available.
faq.urgent.title: Emergency
faq.urgent.numbers.q: Whom should I call in an emergency?
faq.urgent.numbers.a: If you are in danger, call 112 or the appropriate number below. These numbers are also at the bottom of every page.
faq.urgent.service.a: No. The website does not follow requests in real time. In an emergency, call the right number directly. Other useful numbers are on the “Find help by need” page.
faq.pro.title: Professionals
faq.pro.join.q: I represent an organisation: how do we join ADA Pro?
faq.pro.join.a: An organisation applies with its name, its SIRET number and a professional e-mail address. The AccesDirectAide team checks the organisation against an official source before opening its space. When open registration is not available, partner organisations are created by the team and their members are sent a personal invitation.
faq.pro.record.q: Our organisation’s page contains an error.
faq.pro.record.a: Report it from the page, giving the official source that has the correct information. The page is corrected after a check against that source.
faq.beta.title: Public beta
faq.beta.what.a: The website is open to the public and some features are opening gradually. Verified aids, procedures and places can be read now; personal features (account, appointments, messages, documents) open once data protection safeguards are in place.
faq.beta.closed.q: A page says “This feature is not open yet”.
faq.beta.closed.a: It is one of the features that will open later. Nothing is asked of you on that page. You can keep reading the aids, procedures and organisations.
faq.contact.title: Reporting an error, contacting us
faq.contact.report.q: How do I report an error on a page?
faq.contact.report.a: Use the report button at the bottom of the page (during the beta, it opens an e-mail). Say what is wrong and, if possible, give the correct official source.
faq.contact.write.a: Through the Contact page when the form is open. During the public beta, write to the address given in the legal notice. Do not send sensitive personal information.
faq.contact.case.a: AccesDirectAide informs and guides, but does not decide on your case. To be supported in a procedure, go to a place that welcomes the public (CCAS, France Services, association): the directory helps you find one.
guide.search.title: Searching for information
guide.search.s1: Type a few words into the search on the home page or the Search page, for example “student rent”.
guide.search.s2: Choose your municipality to see first what exists near you.
guide.search.s3: If you don’t know what to look for, start from “Find help by need” or “My situation”.
guide.filter.title: Filtering the results
guide.filter.s1: On the Aids page, filter by category, by situation and by area; “Reset filters” clears your choices.
guide.filter.s2: In the directory, filter by type of organisation and by town, and if needed keep only places accessible to people with reduced mobility or those offering online appointments.
guide.filter.s3: In the directory, switch between the list and the map with the “Display” choice.
guide.record.title: Reading a page
guide.record.s1: At the top of the page, “Checked on …” gives the date of the last check against the official source.
guide.record.s2: The “Origin and freshness” block gives the link to the official source: that source is authoritative.
guide.record.s3: The conditions described help you know what to check; only the body concerned decides.
guide.record.s4: You can print the page or save it as a PDF, and report an error at the bottom of the page.
guide.favorites.title: Keeping pages as favourites
guide.favorites.s1: Sign in, then open an aid, procedure or organisation page.
guide.favorites.s3: Find your pages in My favourites; “Remove” takes them off the list.
guide.parcours.title: Following my procedures with My Journey
guide.parcours.s1: On a page, choose “Add to my pathway”: the procedure becomes a step.
guide.parcours.s2: For each step, say where you stand and, if needed, a deadline with its source.
guide.parcours.s3: Sensitive steps (health, disability, residence, justice…) need your explicit consent.
guide.vault.title: Storing my documents in My Vault
guide.vault.s1: Add a PDF, PNG or JPEG document of 3 MB at most, with its expiry date if needed.
guide.vault.s2: Download it or delete it whenever you wish.
guide.vault.s3: Do not upload medical documents until the page offers it.
guide.rdv.title: Booking and managing an appointment
guide.rdv.s1: On the page of an organisation that has opened online booking, choose “See available time slots”.
guide.rdv.s2: Choose a time slot and confirm; some organisations approve each request before confirming it.
guide.rdv.s3: In My appointments, move the appointment (up to 24 hours before, twice at most), cancel it or add it to your calendar.
guide.messages.title: Exchanging messages with an organisation
guide.messages.s1: Open My messages: each conversation is linked to an appointment.
guide.messages.s2: Write your message, read it again, then send it.
guide.messages.s3: Do not write health information or identity numbers: messages are not end-to-end encrypted.
guide.share.title: Sharing a file
guide.share.s1: In My profile, in the section with your files, choose “Manage”.
guide.share.s2: Look for a verified organisation and send it the invitation: it works only once, for 72 hours.
guide.share.s3: “Stop sharing” removes the access whenever you wish.
guide.trusted.title: Inviting a trusted person
guide.trusted.s1: In Trusted persons, invite a relative by e-mail and choose their role.
guide.trusted.s2: Tick what this person can see and for how long (from 30 days to 1 year).
guide.trusted.s3: You see what they have looked at; “End the access” stops it at any time.
guide.helper.title: Getting help with assisted mode
guide.helper.s1: Open Assisted mode, enter the name of the person helping you and the sections you open to them.
guide.helper.s2: Choose the duration (2 hours at most), tick your consent and confirm with your password.
guide.helper.s3: To finish, choose “Stop now (sign out)” or “Continue on my own”.
guide.a11y.title: Adapting the display
guide.a11y.s1: The “Accessibility” button, at the top of the page, sets the text size, the contrast and the line spacing.
guide.a11y.s2: Turn on the easy-to-read version (FALC, in French) when it is offered.
guide.a11y.s3: “Listen to the page” reads the text aloud; the theme button switches between dark and light mode.
guide.languages.title: Changing the language
guide.languages.s1: Choose the language at the top of the page: French, English, Turkish, Arabic, German or Ukrainian.
guide.languages.s2: A page that is not yet translated stays in French; an automatic translation is marked as such.
guide.languages.s3: The French text and the official source are authoritative.
guide.hide.title: Hiding the screen quickly
guide.hide.s1: Press the “Hide the screen” button, or press the Escape key three times.
guide.hide.s2: A dark screen covers the page; click or press Enter to bring it back.
guide.hide.s3: This does not erase your browser history: use private browsing if needed.
guide.compass.title: Asking the Boussole sociale a question
guide.compass.s1: When the assistant is open, open it with its button and write your question in French.
guide.compass.s2: Give your postcode to choose your municipality: answers often depend on the area.
guide.compass.s3: Each answer cites its official sources. The assistant can be wrong: check on the official page.
guide.data.title: Exporting or deleting my data
guide.data.s1: In the account settings, “Download (JSON)” produces a file with your data.
guide.data.s2: In the same place, ask for your account to be deleted: it stays active until the request is processed.
guide.data.s3: The privacy policy explains how your data is used and how to exercise your rights over it.
guide.urgent.title: In an emergency
guide.urgent.s1: If you are in danger, call 112 or the appropriate number: they are also at the bottom of every page.
guide.urgent.s2: AccesDirectAide is not an emergency service: it does not follow requests in real time.
